item.title: The first major The Blood of Dawnwalker update will introduce an easier difficulty option for "people who don't want to experience combat" when it launches in October.
item.description:
The first major The Blood of Dawnwalker update will introduce an easier difficulty option for "people who don't want to experience combat" when it launches in October.
Developer Rebel Wolves' game director, Konrad Tomaszkiewicz, teased the changes coming to the team's breakout vampire RPG during a new interview with Eurogamer. Amongst a batch of combat tweaks and other gameplay changes, one of the highlights for the early October The Blood of Dawnwalker update includes reworked difficulty options for players who don't want to spill too much blood during the story.
When the update launches, players will see the new easier difficulty option replace the current easiest mode, called Story Mode, and adopt its name. The version of the mode currently in the game will seemingly be bumped up a peg and given a new name. The Blood of Dawnwalker currently has four difficulty modes – Story, Fair, Challenging, and Duelist – with next month's addition set to bring the total to five.
"We will introduce an additional difficulty level, but an easier one, because many people are asking for a more easy difficulty," Tomaszkiewicz said. "The Story mode which we have right now will be a different difficulty — we will call it Demanding or something like this — and we will add a new Story mode which will be even easier for people who don't want to experience the combat, they just want to learn the story and go through the game without this gameplay challenge."
How exactly The Blood of Dawnwalker will tackle an easier difficulty mode is unclear. The game director's comment suggests it will cater to those who want to skip combat altogether, though how this will be achieved is unclear. There's no release date for the update just yet, but with its launch set for early October, we won't have to wait too long.
Rebel Wolves is also looking into improving gameplay performance, especially for PC users, as well as a fluid option for players to escape fights if they bite off more than they can chew. Other items on the docket include targeting and the camera. Tomaszkiewicz referenced desires from players to tweak how targeting works for Coen and how the upcoming patch will address that.
"There will be three hits you need to take off this stun," he said. "We will see how people will react to that because, as I said, it can create another bad feel, but we will see. Maybe people will switch between targets fluently and if they want to just stun, it will be fine, and if they want to stun and hit a few times, it will be also fine. We will see."
Everything else set to come to The Blood of Dawnwalker in the October patch has yet to be revealed. Although other features, including new game plus, are confirmed to be in the cards, the team is still charging ahead following its successful launch.
It was released for PC, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X/S September 3 and reached more than 1 million copies sold in just two days. For more on The Blood of Dawnwalker, you can read about how Bandai Namco and Rebel Wolves managed to bring their vision to life on a $40 million budget. You can also learn about how some players are using a mod to bypass one of the game's core mechanics.

item.title: A fan of the Love Nikki – Dress Up Queen mobile dress-up game is going viral for shutting down their informative website after determining that some of the game’s clothing designs were “demonic.”
item.description:
A fan of the Love Nikki – Dress Up Queen mobile dress-up game is going viral for shutting down their informative website after determining that some of the game’s clothing designs were “demonic.”
Nikki’s Info was a fan-made website compiling many of Love Nikki’s clothes, accessories, story guides, update details, and other information. An X/Twitter account for the site was created in 2018, and players could subscribe to the administrator’s Patreon for exclusive game guides and other insights.
Those players are now being offered refunds after the site’s admin announced that they are quitting the game due to their religious beliefs, as described in a now-viral blog post.
The admin published the post after a week of inactivity on the Nikki’s Info website, which has been completely wiped of any information relating to the dress-up game. They explained their absence in the post, saying they had “done some horrible things involving the occult” and that the “devil had then gained such a foothold in my life [that] I was firmly in his grasp.”
“All of this started quite small and personal — but quickly escalated, where in the end I was in a situation where I was in a near-death situation involving police, paramedics, and other people, of whose kindness I am grateful for. I [was] on the precipice of a terrible situation — [I] called out to God for help. He answered. I then continued to practice the occult. Things got worse again and started affecting others, especially my suffering family, in a way I can’t declare publicly,” they wrote.
While the poster confirmed that they are now fine, they expressed some issues with the clothing designs in Love Nikki, finding them to be blasphemous with “demonic” undertones.
“The game features a lot of crosses as dress-up items, which are irreverent to God, the God who so kindly and patiently saved me. The God I love,” they continued. “There’s a lot of them, disproportionately so. Some are mixed in with gothic demonic themes. Such things, though they might seem small, carry consequences and meaning. This is not to say that playing the game directly led to what happened to me. I can say with some degree of certainty, it really was the terrible things I did. But in the ‘back story,’ the various games, books, works of fiction, movies, even music — they are there.
“I have wrestled with this, but ultimately I can’t profit from or promote something which offends my God, my Saviour — therefore the site is now closed. The source code, the data, the domain are not for sale.”
⭐Behind the Seams | [Version 2.0 5-Star Outfits] The Inspirations Behind the Designs pic.twitter.com/KMOoKqvo67
The admin’s post has gone viral within the broader Infinity Nikki community, sparking concerns from players and theories as to what clothing items specifically led them to this conclusion.
Some pointed out the oddness of the situation, given that a fair few designs within the Nikki franchise were directly inspired by figures within the Catholic religion. For example, Love Nikki includes an outfit set that’s essentially a Pope-like ensemble, while the official Infinity Nikki X account shared a graphic with specific details about how the team at Infold approached its Behind Prayers outfit set, saying the Starlight Crown headdress incorporated “imagery of the Virgin Mary.”
For now, commenters are doing their best to help the Nikki’s Info admin, though the situation has sparked no end of curiosity and debate within the world of dress-up games.
Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze.

item.title: Call of Duty YouTuber Tdawgsmitty has started a petition to remove skill-based matchmaking in the FPS franchise following successful Destiny protests.
item.description:
Call of Duty YouTuber Tdawgsmitty has started a petition to remove skill-based matchmaking in the FPS franchise following successful Destiny protests.
The YouTuber has been an outspoken advocate against Call of Duty's SBMM and has tried to make noise on the issue in a variety of ways. Last week, he began tweeting at Xbox CEO Asha Sharma about the matter every day in hopes of getting her attention. Now, he's trying a different way. After seeing Destiny fans successfully rally together to get Bungie to resurrect the sci-fi MMO, Tdawgsmitty decided to try to bring Call of Duty fans together in hopes of a similar outcome.
The YouTuber launched a petition which has gained over 500 signatures in roughly an hour. The call to action aims to get SBMM entirely removed from Call of Duty's unranked lobbies, citing frustrations with the current system and how Activision uses data analysts to develop its matchmaking. Instead, he wants the series to utilize SBMM in the game's ranked play, where players deliberately choose to have a more competitive experience.
"Former Call of Duty developer Brian Bright recently shared that his team’s work on [the canceled Call of Duty game NX1] focused on ping and region," reads the description for the petition. "He also stated that Activision eventually began hiring data scientists who worked with its marketing department to push for more skill-based matchmaking. His statement raises serious questions about how matchmaking priorities evolved.
"For players like us, today’s public matches too often feel like the same competitive experience on repeat. Experimenting with a different weapon, relaxing after work, or playing with friends of different skill levels can become frustrating. When every lobby feels like another test, the fun starts to disappear."
The YouTuber also asked for clearer communication regarding matchmaking and the opportunity for the community to test changes itself. The petition comes roughly a month ahead of Modern Warfare 4's release, which will utilize a divisive SBMM system that was introduced earlier this summer in Black Ops 7. Some feel that Call of Duty's SBMM is too punishing and can result in matches that feel consistently unfair, leading to years of frustrations about the franchise's multiplayer.
Whether a petition can change the mind of Activision remains to be seen, but it's not entirely out of the question. Bungie opted to return to Destiny 2 after killing it earlier this year. There was extreme backlash to the initial decision and players decided to make their voices heard through online protests, which included players choosing to not support Bungie's latest game, Marathon. The developer announced that it will be restoring vaulted content and plans to keep supporting the Destiny franchise, leading to an enthusiastic response from fans. Tdawgsmitty cited this as proof that change is possible.
"This Destiny news is huge for gaming," he said on Twitter. "It shows we can use our voice and effect change. It's time for the COD community to step up and get some much needed changes to the direction its been headed."
If Call of Duty fans can rally together by signing petitions, making their voices heard online, and vote with their wallet, it may very well lead to changes. However, Call of Duty is a massive franchise, and as a result, it may be difficult to make the same kind of dent. IGN spoke with Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's lead multiplayer developers in August and asked about how the studio is approaching SBMM.
"I think it's a conversation that we'll continue to have," said Jacky Reynolds, Multiplayer Design Lead at Infinity Ward. "I don't think it's ever going to be a solved system. There's always going to be new iterations that can be made. I think at the end of the day, yeah, we want players to be able to play and have fun. I think that we want to also make sure that they have variety in their matches. I think it's a conversation that we should continue to have. It's also worth mentioning that Joe and I aren’t directly in charge of matchmaking. We are focused on building cool stuff, but I think we're looking forward to seeing how it all shakes out."
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

item.title: Bloodborne movie producer and YouTuber Jacksepticeye has teased more details about the upcoming animated adaptation after reactions to his involvement were "80% critical."
item.description:
Bloodborne movie producer and YouTuber Jacksepticeye has teased more details about the upcoming animated adaptation after reactions to his involvement were "80% critical."
The famed content creator, whose real name is Seán McLoughlin, touched on his attachment to Sony's animated take on FromSoftware's beloved action game during an interview with 100 Questions with Tom Simmons (via GamesRadar). He took the opportunity to not only tease how his Bloodborne won't retell the story of the franchise's one and only proper installment, but also discussed how fans reacted to his role as its producer.
"Bloodborne, obviously, is my favorite game ever, so when I got that call, part of me is like… obviously I was going to do anything, but I wouldn't have let it go in a direction that I don't think is worthy of the Bloodborne IP," Jacksepticeye explained. Then, when asked if he was feeling the pressure to deliver, he said, "Oh yeah."
"I'd say 80% of the responses were critical of it," he said, referring to his involvement in the animated film. "I don't want to say 'negative,' because a lot of people were just… I would be the same if someone took my beloved IP, that's my favorite, and then some YouTuber's attached to it. It would just make you scratch your head a little bit."
Sony unholstered its plans for an animated R-rated Bloodborne movie back at CinemaCon 2026 in April. For some, the reveal was a bit of a double-edged sword, as begging to see more from FromSoftware's Lovecraftian action-horror universe seemed to deliver a project that came out of left field in more ways than one.
Jacksepticeye, a self-proclaimed Bloodborne fanatic, is in the mix as one of its producers. He's joined by PlayStation Productions and Lyrical Animation. Shortly after its reveal, the YouTuber called the opportunity "a dream come true" and "the honor of my life."
He also acknowledged that a lot of Bloodborne fans were probably surprised to hear his name attached to an official project in that universe. Regardless of the shock, it's not a project he wants anyone to be worried about, saying that he "will fight tooth and nail to make this thing the best it possibly can be."
When asked during the new interview about what fans can look forward to when it comes to the animated movie, Jacksepticeye assured watchers that he's "not trying to be the game."
"I'm not trying to one-up the game, and I'm not trying to compete with it, or tell the same story," he explained. "I'm trying to honor the universe that's there and tell as good a story as I can within it."
He continued, saying he has "quite a bit" of sway in the overall production and direction of the Bloodborne movie. During calls about the project, he said that "people listen to me above most anyone else."
"I'm the one being like, 'This is a good idea. This is a bad idea. We shouldn't do this,'" Jacksepticeye elaborated. "But also, I'm the one greenlighting who gets hired and who we work with to make sure that vetting process is good.
"You don't want to bring on anyone that has no idea what Bloodborne is. In simpler terms, I'm sort of the vibe-checker."
The Bloodborne movie currently has no release date. While we wait to learn more about it, you can check out IGN's original 9.1/10 review of the game. You can also read more about Jacksepticeye's approach to the film.
Photo by John Phillips/BAFTA/Getty Images for BAFTA.

item.title: A Pokémon scalper has reportedly been arrested and trespassed after punching a man in a viral confrontation that resulted in a four-year-old child getting hurt in the chaos.
item.description:
A Pokémon scalper has reportedly been arrested and trespassed after punching a man in a viral confrontation that resulted in a four-year-old child getting hurt in the chaos.
A Target store in Lisbon, Connecticut is at the center of a viral incident that occurred on August 28, 2026. Footage from the ordeal spread across social media in late September, showing two scalpers with a cart full of Pokémon merchandise making their way to the shop’s self-checkout stations.
The person who recorded the footage confronted the duo along with his girlfriend, who submitted the footage to PokéStreetz, an account dedicated to exposing bad behavior within the Pokémon TCG community.
In the footage, the four parties argued about the amount of merchandise the scalpers were making off with; the scalpers themselves proudly said, “Damn straight” that they were checking out with all that merch, rather than abiding by the two-per-person limit enacted by Target, and warned the couple not to touch their shopping cart.
The recorder and his girlfriend continued to follow the scalpers up to a self-checkout station, where one of the scalpers decked the recorder in the face, causing him to drop his phone on the ground. Scuffling can be heard in the background, along with a child crying.
PokéStreetz claimed that the recorder fell into this child, a four-year-old girl, after being punched by the scalper. The girl also reportedly fell in the impact and hurt her elbow; although the recorder “immediately” went to check up on the girl, the scalper fled, allegedly leaving his wallet behind.
🚨 TARGET RESTOCK ENDS WITH A PUNCH & A CHILD GETS HURT?! OH NAAAA 🚨📺 This Morning on PokéStreetz📍 Target — Lisbon, CT📅 August 28, 2026 | ⏰ Around noonThe submitter says she & her boyfriend were fourth or fifth in line when two shoppers ahead allegedly filled their… pic.twitter.com/0b7BpAS3WO
According to the account, the scalper was arrested and trespassed from the Target after he returned to retrieve his wallet. PokéStreetz also claimed that the father of the injured girl called police after staff at Target allegedly declined to take action.
The scuffle was verified by a local TCG player in a Pokémon drops and restocks Facebook Group, who described the situation as a “nightmare.”
“Lisbon Target was a nightmare today,” they wrote. “Needless to say, they are changing some things I believe, also no UFC if anyone was looking for that lol. Someone went and whipped out all the Hops and AH tins, then when they got recorded at the front, they got violent and punched someone in the face. I didn’t get names or anything, but it was not the normal crew, as I am somewhat of a hang-around sometimes, and none of the regulars were there.”
No police records or local reports regarding the scalpers’ supposed arrest and trespassing have been located thus far. The incident is one of several that have broken out amid Pokémon's 30th Anniversary celebrations, where special collaborations, merchandise, and trading card drops have resulted in chaos.
For example, the hype around Pokémon's 30th Anniversary September trading card drop went viral for the sheer amount of customers who lined up outside shops hours before launch, with some camping outside, while others ‘reserved’ their spots with ‘ghost chairs’ as crowds of fans vied for the chance at snagging some packs.
Luckily, the powers that be seem to have made enough cards to go around this time, and it’s hurting scalpers; a scalping Discord group made the rounds on social media after moaning that the excessive stock was hurting their businesses.
Image Credit: Kindel Media, The Pokemon Company

item.title: Take-Two Interactive, the parent company of Rockstar Games, has begun taking down videos and posts about leaked GTA 5 and GTA 6 content.
item.description:
Take-Two Interactive, the parent company of Rockstar Games, has begun taking down videos and posts about leaked GTA 5 and GTA 6 content.
Last week, a ton of files for Grand Theft Auto 5 leaked online. These were reportedly obtained during the 2022 hack, which also resulted in the first-ever footage of GTA 6 leaking online. These files have been rumored for some time, but are only just now surfacing publicly. They include cut dialogue from GTA 5, which also seems to hint at different outcomes for the story, such as a darker ending for Franklin. However, the two biggest things are details of a scrapped Liberty City expansion for GTA 5 and an extremely early version of GTA 6's map.
Given that this material was illegally obtained in a hack and not officially released by Rockstar or datamined through the game's files, the studio's parent company, Take-Two Interactive, is working to scrub the assets from the internet. Various YouTube videos and posts with visuals of the leaked material or clips of the audio have been taken down by Take-Two. It doesn't seem like the company is going scorched-earth like it did for the GTA 6 leaks, but it does appear that content creators who post this material are at risk of copyright strikes.
Take-Two are now taking down YouTube videos regarding the latest #GTA leaks. My video only covered a list of files, a visualisation of the data from one of the files using a fan made tool and one cut piece of GTA V dialogue.Nothing regarding #GTAVI. The dialogue is probably the… pic.twitter.com/gbaKt2kcX5
We're just two months away from the release of GTA 6, and it's likely that Rockstar's security is going to be at an all-time high. The studio has been compromised by multiple leaks for the last four years, and now it's at a point where the game is likely finished and could be at risk of being spoiled. However, the lack of physical copies will make it a lot harder for things to leak ahead of its release. Given tons of footage managed to surface in August, though, it's not impossible for more things to make their way online.
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

item.title: An indie game developer has accused a fellow dev of using AI to rip off his game, a first-person, physics-based title where players peel potatoes.
item.description:
An indie game developer has accused a fellow dev of using AI to rip off his game, a first-person, physics-based title where players peel potatoes.
Independent game developer Rado Klasa is going viral after pointing out a glaring similarity between his game, called 1,000,000 Potatoes, and another title named Potato Please. Both have a similar premise; players peel potatoes using physics-based engines. Each game takes place in a Soviet-style military setting. They both seem horror-adjacent.
Klasa posted about his game back in July; on September 20, game consultant Indie Game Joe shared a trailer for Golden Horn Studios’ Potato Please. It didn’t take long for Klasa to come across the post, prompting him to speak out about what he is calling blatant intellectual theft.
made a dumb little game where you peel 1,000,000 potatoes by hand in a cold soviet warehouse. thought it would take a weekend.potato 15 had a tooth in it. i kept going.#screenshotsaturday #indiegame pic.twitter.com/WBXx2XRqeI
Klasa believes that Golden Horn directly stole the idea for his game and accused them of using artificial intelligence to do so, describing the situation as “every indie dev’s worst nightmare.”
“I created this concept for the GMTK game jam,” he explained. “I held off on my Steam page to obsessively polish the mechanics... and it just got cloned and shipped. Probably mostly with a simple AI prompt.”
“I’ve spent time refining the game feel, controls, and details,” he added. “It hurts to see a rushed clone beat me to market, but I refuse to let a cheap copy win. The original version will always have the quality players actually deserve.”
It’s every indie dev's worst nightmare.I created this concept for the GMTK game jam. I held off on my Steam page to obsessively polish the mechanics... and it just got cloned and shipped. Probably mostly with a simple AI prompt.Here’s my original build vs theirs 👇 https://t.co/4Ri1y0R3J6
Curators on Steam are already flagging Potato Please as an “AI imagery Rip off of 1,000,000 Potatoes,” and commenters on social media are offering their support and promising to wishlist Klasa’s game — but Golden Horn is maintaining their innocence.
“We need to address this directly. Calling our game a ‘clone’ and implying it was made with ‘a simple AI prompt’ are serious accusations,” the studio wrote in response to Klasa’s post on X/Twitter. “We had never seen your game before these posts. Potato Please originated independently from a potato meme and video popular in our community.
“Similar concepts are not evidence of copying. Real people have spent significant time designing, modelling, coding and developing this game, and we’re prepared to show our project files and development process if necessary. We’re happy to discuss genuine similarities, but publicly presenting speculation about our team and our work as fact is unfair.”
We need to address this directly. Calling our game a “clone” and implying it was made with “a simple AI prompt” are serious accusations.We had never seen your game before these posts. Potato Please originated independently from a potato meme and video popular in our community.…
Players, however, aren’t convinced of Golden Horn’s story. “Its’ just really f**king weird that somehow you both got Soviet Russia potato peeling sim and your account didn't exist until after the game jam happened,” one user argued.
“This is literally 1:1 the SAME GAME lmao stop lying,” another wrote, while others couldn't seem to uncover the viral meme Golden Horn referenced in its reply.
Still, others have accused Golden Horn of using AI to write their response to Klasa’s post. Potato Please made their account just two months ago, and thus far, have shared no progress videos or screenshots showing them making the game, though this isn’t totally unusual in itself.
For other unique indie games that haven’t been hit with AI allegations, check out our coverage of Stray Dog: nobody cares and Ylem’s Cat, both games where you play as an animal or fight bad guys alongside an animal.

item.title: Daredevil: Born Again will reportedly end with its upcoming third season.
item.description:
Daredevil: Born Again will reportedly end with its upcoming third season.
According to The Hollywood Reporter, Daredevil: Born Again will not return for a fourth season. Disney reportedly made the decision following the end of production on the third season, suggesting the show wasn't necessarily designed to end here. Additionally, THR reports that the Marvel series' showrunner, Dario Scardapane, exited the project during post-production. Sources reportedly raised eyebrows at the departure, as it has left the show without a clear leader to finish it. Daredevil: Born Again Season 3 is currently expected to premiere in 2027.
It's unclear if Daredevil: Born Again was canceled or if it truly is just the end of this story. The series wasn't a smash hit when it came to ratings, but was hailed as a success by critics and fans, especially compared to other Marvel shows. Disney has pulled back on Marvel TV series in recent years following a string of mediocre releases, but is still committed to a small handful moving forward. The next Marvel show will be VisionQuest, releasing on October 14. THR also noted that three to five other shows are in development, including a spy series named Zodiac.
Wonder Man was also canceled earlier this summer, despite getting greenlit for a second season. As of right now, it's unclear what Daredevil's future is in the MCU. Fans have wanted to see him in a film, especially after his brief cameo in Spider-Man: No Way Home. As Spidey continues to embrace street-level battles, a Daredevil crossover in the next film could be extremely fruitful.
This is also the second time the Man Without Fear has had his TV time cut short at the third season. Netflix and Marvel pulled the plug on the original Daredevil series in 2018 following a critically-acclaimed third season. A fourth season was expected to follow, but various issues prevented that from happening, such as Disney trying to launch its own streamer with original programming. It took the better part of a decade to get Daredevil back on screen, but fans were excited once it finally happened, particularly because it continued the story of the original show and leveraged its darker tone.
Is this the end of Matt Murdock's journey in the MCU? Only time will tell, but we hope that's not the case.
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

item.title: Blizzard has confirmed its open-world StarCraft shooter "won't be exclusive" to Xbox platforms when it launches in 2030.
item.description:
Blizzard Entertainment has confirmed its open-world StarCraft shooter "won't be exclusive" to Xbox platforms when it launches in 2030.
Representatives for the World of Warcraft developer shared the update for the far-off franchise revival in a series of post-BlizzCon 2026 email exchanges with Kotaku. It's an update that slightly widens what will be StarCraft's list of launch platforms – but where exactly it will be available isn't so simple.
When Blizzard announced its new game with the "Dominion" cinematic trailer at BlizzCon, it neglected to share how exactly players will be able to play it in 2030. Although previous entries in the RTS series have traditionally been available on PC, the only real platform confirmation we've received thus far came from Xbox UK, which promised that an "Xbox console" release was planned.
Kotaku asked for clarification and was told that Blizzard "can only say for now that StarCraft won't be exclusive." The site then asked if the lack of exclusivity meant the game would come to additional consoles, or if it simply meant it would receive a PC release. Representatives for the developer said that, if a story were to call StarCraft an Xbox-exclusive, they would need to issue a correction request.
In other words, with at least four years left of development, Blizzard is keeping mum. While its response is far from a specific answer, it's not nothing, either. The Microsoft-owned game developer won't say if players on PlayStation or maybe even Nintendo Switch 2 will be able to pick up a copy, but straying from the exclusivity language means the plan is for Blizzard to support at least one other platform.
It's worth noting that, when we're talking about games coming out four whole years from now, we don't really know what the console gaming space will even look like. Microsoft is still chipping away at the mysterious family of devices under the Project Helix banner behind the scenes, with some expecting it to launch as soon as next year. Sony may not know when the PlayStation 6 is coming out, but it will presumably be in players' hands by that point, too.
A four-year wait means there's lots of ground to cover, and knowing so little about what exactly StarCraft is only makes it harder to peer into the future. Blizzard announced the long-rumored video game just a little more than a week ago and only really shared that cinematic trailer at the time. The year 2030 might feel like the distant future, but the release window is still one that the team feels confident about.

item.title: Speaking with IGN Japan at Tokyo Game Show, Final Fantasy 7 Revelation director Naoki Hamaguchi said the game will contain an option to let players automatically level up their characters, allowing them experience the story without needing to grind — but the broader gaming community is at odds with this idea.
item.description:
Speaking with IGN Japan at Tokyo Game Show 2026, Final Fantasy 7 Revelation director Naoki Hamaguchi said the game will contain an option to let players automatically level up their characters, allowing them to experience the story without needing to grind — but the broader gaming community is at odds with this idea.
Final Fantasy 7 Revelation, like every other game in the series, is very narrative-focused. Luckily, there’ll be a feature for those who want to breeze through tough battles and get to its major story beats, as told by Hamaguchi at TGS 2026.
During our conversation, he told us that he’d received feedback from players who claimed they had a hard time getting through the previous games’ main story due to being underleveled, saying they didn’t want to grind through the wealth of side quests to work their way up to a higher level.
"Naturally, because we've prepared so much side content, [a player's] level might not quite reach the requirement for the main story. There were voices [from players] saying, 'Even though you say I don't have to do the side content, if I don't do it and make my characters stronger, I end up struggling,’” he explained.
"For people who really just want to do the main story, we've included an option that asks, if your level is not high enough for the recommended level when you reach a part of the main story, 'Would you like to automatically raise [your level] to the recommended level?’”
This particular remark has sparked a heated debate within the gaming community. The broad sentiment from critics argues that adding such a feature makes the game far too ‘hand-holdy,’ and furthermore, presents a startling implication that young players are no longer being faced with challenges in games.
Veteran game artist TheCartelDel provided the most viral argument against adding this feature, writing on X/Twitter, “We need to have a serious discussion about how games used to be a unique method to teach kids and teens about patience, delayed gratification, and working hard to accomplish a goal — and now we're designing away the need to persevere at all. You will learn to overcome nothing.”
“I like the FF7 remakes. I really do. But every piece of news I’ve been seeing about Revelation feels like they’re accommodating this game for people who don’t like playing games and it’s embarrassing,” another user said.
“Having options to FACILITATE the experience is ALWAYS good, but there's a difference between facilitating and ELIMINATING the experience,” another argued. “In an RPG, getting lost in its world, exploring, fighting, and leveling up is precisely the nature of the genre.”
We need to have a serious discussion about how games used to be a unique method to teach kids & teens about patience, delayed gratification, and working hard to accomplish a goal - and now we're designing away the need to persevere at all. You will learn to overcome nothing. https://t.co/K0FOtDxa5n
That being said, FF7 Revelation is going to be a massive game, with Hamaguchi teasing that it’ll take completionists “at least 100 hours” to totally finish. It’s an open-world game, after all, with a wide variety of side quests to complete and areas to explore. That’s why there’s a few ways players can navigate its world, either by dropping in from the Highwind (thanks for the ride, Cid) or traversing the landscape via Chocobo — or heck, even walking on foot.
Because such a massive open world can trigger decision fatigue from players who prefer a more linear experience, Hamaguchi said the development team is working hard to find a balance between providing enough guidance for those who struggled in exploration and those who want to wander off on their own, saying he’d received some feedback calling the game a bit too hand-holdy.
“There are people who want to explore, and there are people who don't want to get lost. So, I think that for open-world games today, you need quite a thorough level of guidance. However, on the other hand, there were also opinions from people who wanted to discover things on their own, saying that the guidance was a bit intrusive or in the way. So, we are currently considering things like toggling that guidance on and off,” he said.
Either way, it appears that Hamaguchi is well-aware of concerns that the game will do too much heavy lifting on players’ behalf. It’s also worth noting that many AAA games these days offer difficulty levels specifically tailored to experiencing their story modes, so Hamaguchi’s automatic level-up option isn’t something totally new.
What’s your take on this feature? Do you think it’s heralding an issue with the next generation of games, or do you think the conversation has been blown out of proportion? Let us know in the comments below.
Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze.

item.title: The next-generation Nvidia graphics cards have reportedly been delayed to 2028, according to known Nvidia leaker Kopite7Kimi on Twitter.
item.description:
We're nearly two years out from the RTX 5090 launching at CES 2025, and if everything was normal, Nvidia would likely be getting ready to release its next generation of graphics cards at CES 2027, but it doesn't look like that's going to happen.
The next-generation Nvidia graphics cards, likely based on the Rubin architecture, have reportedly been delayed to 2028, according to known Nvidia leaker Kopite7Kimi on Twitter. This isn't the first time Nvidia has been reported to either delay or cancel a graphics card in the last year, either. Back in February, the same leaker suggested that Nvidia's typical mid-generation Super refresh was also canceled, thanks to increased demand for GPUs and memory for AI data centers.
I hope Jensen can see everyone's passion and launch new products for gaming as soon as possible. Unfortunately, GR20x is a product from 2028. That means they have postponed again. 🙃🙃🙃I will try to minimize updates until there is definite news. (Lessons learned)
It is important to keep in mind, though, that leaks for Nvidia's next-generation graphics cards are all over the place. Just last week, YouTuber Moore's Law is Dead cited nebulous sources inside Nvidia, suggesting that the Rubin-based RTX 6000 graphics cards would be launching sometime in the first half of 2027.
You should take both of these leaks with a grain of salt, but Nvidia delaying its next-generation graphics cards to 2028 would make a lot of sense. After all, the flagship GeForce RTX 5090 is now commanding prices around $9,000, despite launching for $1,999 last year.
The RTX 5090 isn't the only GPU going up in price, either. We're now 10 months into RAMageddon, and it's unlikely to end any time soon. Thanks to that ongoing shortage, every graphics card on the market is much more expensive now than it was a year ago. Even without that happening in the background, Nvidia would probably raise the price on its next-generation graphics cards, but now that memory and GPU costs have gone through the roof, I shudder to think how expensive the RTX 6080 would even be.
Nvidia has also dropped the gaming category from its earnings reports, lumping GeForce in with the 'Edge Computing' category, along with robotics. In its recent Q2 2027 earnings report, Nvidia didn't even mention gaming, instead focusing on the mountains of money it's making from AI. So, Team Green is likely also in no rush to get new consumer graphics cards out there.
Only time will tell whether or not Nvidia has anything up its sleeves for gamers next year, but if it's anything like 2026 so far, we're likely just going to get more software tricks – not that that's necessarily a bad thing.
Jackie Thomas is the Senior Tech Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. She's been covering gaming hardware for more than a decade for IGN, TechRadar, Gizmodo, PC Gamer and more. You can follow her @Jackiecobra

item.title: Through all of the uncertainty and livestream chat takeovers, Bungie has confirmed more Destiny is coming, and fans can't believe it.
item.description:
Through all of the uncertainty and livestream chat takeovers, Bungie has confirmed more Destiny is coming, and fans can't believe it.
In case you missed it, the Sony-owned game developer confirmed earlier today that more Destiny "stories and games" are on the way just four months after it launched the final major update for Destiny 2. Content is in the process of being unvaulted, too, with the studio promising that the long-running sci-fi shooter franchise remains "foundational" to its future.
Today, we’re sharing more about the future of Bungie, including our plans for Destiny, Marathon, and how we’re changing the way we work. Read more on https://t.co/ZkmLWmaQZr: https://t.co/QbDwADGinr pic.twitter.com/F5tcXF0TsN
Calling this a change of tune would be an understatement. Sony and Bungie announced in May of this year that the Monument of Triumph update would be the last major Destiny 2 update when it launched in June. While the content drop did manage to bring a significant spike in players as fans pleaded for the studio to not abandon the IP, no news of any future Destiny projects was ever announced, and before today, it didn't seem like it ever would be. Bungie does have Marathon to worry about, after all.
There was next to no reason to suspect the campaign to save Destiny would ever be successful. So, when Bungie made its announcement today, explicitly mentioning how fans directly impacted its decision to commit to more Destiny content, everyone lost their minds.
"Bungie would not be what it is today without Destiny and the vibrant community that has rallied around it for more than a decade," the studio said in a post on its website today. "When we announced that Monument of Triumph would be the final content update to Destiny 2, you responded in force. Your voices mattered, and the way you showed up made a real impact. You reminded everyone how much this world, its history, and its future still mean to you."
Somehow, Destiny has returned, and at least based on today's announcement, players can thank themselves for making it happen. Social media is currently flooded with reactions from the more vocal campaigners and the ones who never thought their efforts would make a difference. It's a different kind of triumph that players didn't expect, even if it's unclear when exactly they'll see more content arrive.
"Holy s**t. We actually f**king won!" Destiny and Warframe content creator My name is Byf said. "They're un-vaulting content, and are making moves to create more Destiny in the future! We actually did the thing! We made our own fate!"
"DESTINY BACK FROM THE DEAD?????" YouTuber MrRoflWaffles said.
"I’m actually crying I don’t even know how to express how happy this makes me," Bungie fan and streamer VesselOfTauCeti said. "Destiny has a future again. Marathon is expanding beyond its genre. The future right now looks bright."
@DestinyTheGame rn pic.twitter.com/co1N47Gs7t
Unvaulting pre-Shadowkeep content let's go Hopefully Sony greenlights Destiny 3 pic.twitter.com/1hppIwG6C1
Historic day! Holy W! pic.twitter.com/dYuO6C8zqS
Let's take a brief look at how the internet responded after Bungie announced plans to cease live support for Destiny 2. The initial reaction was intense, with players taking to social media to both question the decision and express concern for the studio as a whole. Instead of dying down, the campaign really only intensified from there.
Marathon was hit with a review-bombing campaign from disappointed Destiny fans in May. Players then almost immediately planned and executed a server takeover that resulted in Destiny 2's highest concurrent player peak in two years. While the average player helped swarm both Sony and non-Sony livestream chats, developers from completely different games voiced their support for Bungie and the Destiny fans who were being left behind.
Some members of the Bungie team have also taken to X/Twitter to share their thoughts on a return to Destiny content. Other developers from across the industry have also chimed in.
Bungie says "we are not done with Destiny." pic.twitter.com/ZYFV3D35iL
https://t.co/dB2hin3tZw pic.twitter.com/MbOv7VW90a
"A big update, from the heart, coming from our leaders," Bungie principal comms manager Dylan Gafner said. "Know you'll have a lot of questions after watching the video and reading the blog. Destiny. Marathon. Bungie. Throw 'em our way. Cheers to the future. Guardians make their own fate."
"These guys have made it incredibly easy to be excited about my job," Bungie senior gameplay designer Danny Nanni said. "If you've not watched how they're moving us forward, I recommend you do!"
"Love everything about this, rooting for the studio hard," Overwatch senior designer Dylan Snyder said, ending a message with a heart emoji. "Games are better with a healthy Bungie in the space, and with Destiny around and cooking. Ggs."
For now, what exactly Destiny's future looks like is unclear. What has fans talking today, though, is the fact that it even has one to look forward to. The studio has had a rough year, with layoffs announced in June later revealed to have affected hundreds of staff. The company confirmed it would be subleasing parts of its massive Bellevue, Washington headquarters earlier this month.
Michael Cripe is a freelance writer with IGN. He's best known for his work at sites like The Pitch, The Escapist, and OnlySP. Be sure to give him a follow on Bluesky (@mikecripe.bsky.social) and Twitter (@MikeCripe).

item.title: Rockstar Games has outlined its policy for modding ahead of Grand Theft Auto 6's release, and it may crush the dreams of some would-be entrepreneurs.
item.description:
Rockstar Games has outlined its policy for modding ahead of Grand Theft Auto 6's release, and it may crush the dreams of some would-be entrepreneurs.
Rockstar Games has a somewhat contentious history with the modding community, but the developer has lightened up in recent years following the absurd success of GTA 5's RP community. Rockstar even acquired the developer of the FiveM modding platform and partnered with the biggest RP server, nopixel, to develop a new iteration. Now, it seems like Rockstar is trying to make it clear where it stands with modding ahead of GTA 6's release, so there's less room for controversy when modding inevitably begins.
The rules are clearly outlined on Rockstar's website and include some obvious examples, such as no use of others' IP, pornography, bullying, or endorsements of violent extremism. Additionally, modders can not make Rockstar's games available on platforms they've never been released on, and they can't add characters, maps, or assets from other games to different titles, either.
There is one section of the policy that seems to specifically address some things that influencers have been planning for some time: Rockstar explicitly forbids unauthorized commercialization of mods in its games.
For instance, influencers like Adin Ross have spent the last couple of years making claims that he'd create a GTA 6 server where players could essentially live inside of it and earn real money. Ross even went as far as saying players could quit their jobs in real life and live off the money made in his GTA 6 server. Unless Rockstar signs off on it, though, that won't be possible. Rockstar's policy notes that players can not exchange real money in mods via crypto or traditional currencies. Players also can't use real money for gambling within modded content, and mod owners can not promote any kind of third-party sponsored content.
Ultimately, it sounds like the servers that Ross and other influencers have been imagining will not be possible. As folks have probably anticipated, GTA 6 will not be a Second Life experience to make real money. It's still very much a video game, and one over which Rockstar plans to have close supervision. There's a lot of room for the game to get corrupted if influencers could radically commercialize their servers, so it's probably best that Rockstar is policing this.
We won't see any mods for GTA 6 for a while, as the game isn't releasing on PC on November 19. However, there have been a variety of teases from Rockstar's parent company, Take-Two Interactive, that GTA 6 will eventually make its way to PC. How long will that take? We have no idea. It seems hard to imagine it being any later than a year, given the increased popularity of PC gaming since Rockstar's last major release and the high demand for this game, though.
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

item.title: We got the chance to speak with Yoshiaki Kawajiri, director of the cult-classic anime film Ninja Scroll, who opened up about his creative process and explained why he hasn’t made a new movie in nearly two decades as Ninja Scroll prepares for its 4K theatrical re-release.
item.description:
We got the chance to speak with Yoshiaki Kawajiri, director of the cult-classic anime film Ninja Scroll, who opened up about his creative process and explained why he hasn’t made a new movie in nearly two decades as Ninja Scroll prepares for its 4K theatrical re-release.
Yoshiaki Kawajiri is a legend in the anime industry. Fans might know him best from Ninja Scroll and Vampire Hunter D: Bloodlust, but he’s also the mind behind other genre-defining works like Goku: Midnight Eye, Wicked City, and Demon City Shinjuku, to name just a few.
However, he hasn’t taken the helm on a project in almost 20 years. With Ninja Scroll getting a 4K theatrical re-release in October, we had to ask him why he hasn’t brought his iconic art style and signature pulpy flair to a new film in some time.
His answer likely isn’t all that surprising; at 75 years old, Kawajiri isn’t the spring chicken he used to be. He’s also pretty particular about his creative vision, so managing a film or series and making sure it would stay faithful to his overall goal would take too much out of him.
“I am the type of person who cannot leave a work entirely in someone else's hands, so at my age, and given my physical stamina, directing is no longer possible for me,” he told us.
Nowadays, Kawajiri is focused on supporting roles, boasting oodles of credits for storyboarding standout anime series like Beastars, Frieren: Beyond Journey’s End, and Jujutsu Kaisen. For Kawajiri, the process of storyboarding hinges on a very specific requirement: it must be interesting to him.
“I approach the script and storyboards with the understanding that the most important point is how to keep the audience interested. I cannot work on storyboards unless I find the work interesting. In other words, my curiosity is my greatest weapon. More recently, Frieren and Beastars were projects that I really enjoyed working on,” he said.
There’s been a massive shift in the anime industry between Kawajiri’s heyday and now. A quick look on social media will reveal scores of fans bemoaning the quality of modern animation and yearning for the high-detail fluidity of older works. Kawajiri, however, doesn’t believe nostalgia is a driving factor in this sentiment; instead, he believes fans want high-quality anime, regardless of what era it comes from.
“I don't think it is nostalgia. Truly excellent and entertaining works never lose their appeal, no matter how many years pass! And creators who make such works will certainly continue to emerge in the future,” he said.
“Personally, I believe the biggest change [in the industry] was the emergence of original video animation in the 1980s, which expanded the diversity of works while creating an environment where creators could express their individuality. There is no doubt that this became one of the factors that helped Japanese anime grow into compelling content that spread around the world. …The history of Japanese manga and anime is unique, and that long history has produced countless outstanding works. I am very proud that those works are now being embraced around the world.”
Kawajiri has no doubt created, or helped create, many of those works, and one of them is making its way back to theaters this fall. Ninja Scroll got a major facelift thanks and was restored to 4K thanks to hours of painstaking work from dedicated staff members and oversight from Kawjiri.
“By focusing on reproducing the original beauty and richness of the cels and background artwork, without compromising the atmosphere of the work or the texture of the film grain, I believe the result has an even more powerful look and feel. However, since this was an analog production filmed 30 years ago, there is no doubt that the process of removing scratches, dirt, and dust from the cels was an extremely painstaking task for the staff,” he said.
“I hope longtime fans will enjoy the even more powerful visuals brought to life by the 4K remaster, and I promise that those seeing it for the first time will say, ‘A great work is still great, even after 30 years!’ I hope you enjoy it! Thank you for loving Ninja Scroll!”
Iconic Events Releasing and AMC Global Media's HDIVE are bringing Ninja Scroll to select theaters across the United States and Canada for a limited release on October 4, 5, and 7. You can purchase tickets at participating theaters on the Iconic Releasing website linked here.
Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze.

item.title: The Steam Deck has been around for four years at this point, and while I mostly use it to play Ball x Pit while I watch TV, scientists at Airbus in the UK have used it to test the the ExoMars Rover.
item.description:
The Steam Deck has been around for four years at this point, and while I mostly use it to play Ball x Pit while I watch TV, scientists at Airbus in the UK have used it to test the the ExoMars Rover.
In a video published by YouTuber Tom Scott, an Airbus senior engineer walks him through progress on the new rover, which is being tested in a simulated Mars setting. Ultimately, this rover will be controlled autonomously through mounted 3D cameras thanks to the distance between Mars and Earth, but for now, it has to be controlled locally with a computer.
Initially, she gives the prototype rover instructions through a laptop, telling it to go forward. Later on in the video, Scott is handed a Steam Deck that's running some kind of custom program, which allows him to control a different prototype rover in real time thanks to the controller that's built into the handheld.
Unfortunately, the video doesn't go into a lot of detail about what's actually being run on the Steam Deck, but it isn't the first time Valve's handheld has been used to control robotics; a couple of years ago, fans spotted Disney operators using the Steam Deck to control droids at Galaxy's Edge. Due to the open nature of Valve's hardware, it's likely that the Steam Deck is being used for all kinds of things we don't know about.
That's a fate that's probably going to be shared for the Steam Machine and Steam Frame as well. All of these devices are running on Linux and make no effort to stop users from installing different programs or even operating systems, so it's only natural that they're being used for things other than gaming.
Back when I interviewed Valve engineers Pierre-Loup Griffais and Yazan Aldehayyat for the Steam Machine, they seemed completely open to this, with Aldehayyat telling me, "I don't think it's a coincidence that a good PC is also a good gaming device. At the end of the day, good hardware is good hardware. So in a lot of ways, the challenges you're trying to solve are, a lot of them are pretty much the same." I'm sure that Valve didn't envision the Steam Deck being used to test Mars rovers, but it's still in the spirit of people finding different ways to use the hardware.
The side effect of the Deck, Machine, and Frame being open for things other than gaming is that the hardware is more expensive. Because Valve doesn't lock down its hardware at all, there's nothing stopping scientists from buying Steam Decks just because they happen to be great for controlling robotics, rather than buying and playing games from the Steam store.
It's going to be especially interesting to see the different ways the Steam Frame is used in the future. I can only imagine what scientists will be able to do with an open VR headset with all kinds of motion-tracking capabilities. If the Steam Deck is being used to control Mars Rovers, just imagine what the Steam Frame will be able to do.
Jackie Thomas is the Senior Tech Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. She's been covering gaming hardware for more than a decade for IGN, TechRadar, Gizmodo, PC Gamer and more. You can follow her @Jackiecobra

item.title: After being asked about a stage show production, such as what Game of Thrones is experimenting with, The Witcher creator has said he is "open to suggestions" for future adaptations, not ruling out unconventional formats for the fantasy series, and pointing to previous Witcher musical productions in Poland.
item.description:
From musicals to whatever comes next, The Witcher creator, Andrzej Sapkowski, isn't ruling out even more unconventional ways of bringing the fantasy series to life.
The Witcher has already been adapted into just about every major format you could think of, from the immensely popular video games and Netflix's live-action series to animated films and comics.
But during our recent wide-ranging interview with Sapkowski and his English translator, David French, we asked the author whether there are more experimental formats he'd like to see The Witcher explore, such as the possibility of a major stage production like Game of Thrones.
"Does a musical count as a stage play?" he asked. "If so, there were already two. What else? I am open to suggestions. Even unconventional ones."
Yes, Geralt of Rivia has, in fact, already ventured into musical territory, although Sapkowski seemingly doesn't want to put a limit on what could come next either. After all, the franchise has spent years expanding far beyond the books that first introduced Geralt.
Plus, there's certainly no shortage of Witcher projects on the horizon, either. CD Projekt Red's The Witcher 3: Remastered is due to arrive on September 29, while the surprise new expansion Songs of the Past is planned for 2027. The Witcher 4, meanwhile, is currently targeting a 2028 release and will put Ciri in the starring role.
The publishing side of the franchise is also expanding further, with full-cast audio drama adaptations of Sapkowski's books arriving through 2026 and 2027, beginning with Crossroads of Ravens before moving on to The Last Wish and Sword of Destiny.
Netflix's live-action The Witcher is also heading into its fifth and final season, now expected in 2027 after a supposed delay.
If you want to listen to The Witcher Full Cast Audiobooks, we recommend checking out this new Audible deal as part of the upcoming Prime Day sale. Amazon Prime members can sign up for four months of Audible Standard for just $0.99 per month.
Of course, Sapkowski himself isn't slowing down either. The author has confirmed that he is already writing his next Witcher novel, with a targeted completion date of 2027.
He has also told IGN that he is also considering eventually returning to the short-story format that originally introduced many readers to Geralt, while suggesting there is still plenty of room to explore the Witcher's earlier years.
Whether that next novel ultimately brings us another glimpse of young Geralt remains to be seen, but Sapkowski's response when we asked whether there was more room to explore that period of his life was short but sweet: "Room? Sky is the limit."
Robert Anderson is a Senior Commerce Editor for IGN. Based in London, UK, he is a qualified journalist with a Bachelor of Arts in Journalism (First Class Degree) and over seven years of professional writing and editing experience.
You can usually find Robert lost in open-world RPG games like Elden Ring and Cyberpunk 2077. Outside of gaming, his passions include reading comics (especially Superman, Batman, and Spider-Man), taking photos, and keeping up with the latest in film and TV.
His primary coverage focuses on tracking down the best gaming deals and diving into the fast-paced world of Trading Card Games (TCGs). He regularly covers everything from the latest releases in Pokémon TCG and the most expensive cards to comprehensive Magic: The Gathering buying guides.

item.title: Pokémon scalpers are complaining that the franchise's new 30th Anniversary set has been too generous with its rare cards — leaving resellers unable to generate their usual profits.
item.description:
Pokémon scalpers are complaining that the franchise's new 30th Anniversary set has been too generous with its rare cards — leaving resellers unable to generate their usual profits.
Last week saw the long-awaited 30th Anniversary Pokémon Trading Card game set go on sale, with the usual scramble for stock among scalpers looking to make a quick profit. We reported on long lines outside stores in the U.S., plus frustration over "ghost chairs" left outside for days. In the U.K., there were ructions after accusations that a minor celebrity had ignored purchase limits and skipped the queue to snaffle up supply.
But as the dust settled, collectors quickly found that the 30th Anniversary set's rare cards... actually weren't that rare. Indeed, it appears that The Pokémon Company has done its best to defeat the usual scalper market by making all of the set's main cards findable with relative ease.
The only cards now being resold in the low thousands of dollars are the three eye-wateringly colored Red, Green and Blue Mew cards, which do seem to have a low drop rate. Otherwise, resale prices dip to well under $250 for everything else. Most of the top 15 expensive cards have been judged as being worth around $100 or less — a far cry from the thousands of dollars seen in previous sets.
This is great news for most fans, who will be able to fill their binders with the majority of cards — rather than a good chunk being left well beyond reach. However, it's less great news for scalpers who invested thousands of dollars in buying up stock expecting to make a huge margin.
"2-3 years ago, quite literally on this subreddit, many people were anticipating the 30th anniversary as a bull catalyst for exit strategies for their investments," complained one collector on dedicated reddit /r/PokeInvesting. "The literal complete opposite happened."
"It'll crush even more when more and more people start dumping," wrote another collector. "It's gonna be a bloody mess."
Not everyone is upset, however. In another /r/PokeInvesting thread, one fan has suggested that the 30th Anniversary set's easy hit rates were good for money-making in the long-term. Why? Because more children and potential collectors will be lured in by the high rate of rare cards this time around — only for things to inevitably be reversed in future.
"I actually think this set is extremely healthy for the hobby long term," TommyC6852 wrote. "This is a set that is a blast to open; and should be decently available for the common collector. At some point you want people to have fun; and this set should give the hobby the breath of fresh air that it needs. The more fun people have, the longer they stay in. The longer people stay engaged; the higher our investments will go."
The next Pokémon trading card set, Mega Evolution — Delta Reign, will launch as soon as November.
Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

item.title: Bungie Studio Head Poria Torkan and Josh Dean, Head of Product and GM of Marathon, revealed plans to “evolve” Marathon as Bungie continues to navigate big internal changes.
item.description:
Bungie Studio Head Poria Torkan, alongside the Head of Product and GM of Marathon, Josh Dean, revealed plans to “evolve” Marathon as Bungie continues to navigate big internal changes.
In a September 21 video message to fans, Torkan and Dean addressed what’s next for Marathon, saying the game is an “important part” of shaping where Bungie goes next.
"It didn’t reach as many players as we’d hoped,” Torkan admitted. “But we also know and understand that the game needs to evolve.”
“We’re gonna anchor on what makes Marathon special and evolve it beyond the genre constraints that we’ve placed on it. We’re going to expand Marathon into a deeper survival experience that gives players more ways to take on its dangerous alien world,” Dean continued.
He outlined the team's goal for Marathon by the end of year one, saying that Bungie hopes to "preserve what you already love, but find ways to provide players with more agency in how you play, whether in PvE or PvP."
This news follows Bungie's plans to delay Marathon's next big update from late September to December. In a blog post published at the same time as Torkan and Dean's video message, Bungie reiterated that it "still [has] a lot planned for [its] October Nightfall Refresh and Symbiosis update in December." It also promised that players will get more Marathon news "later this week" regarding their vision for the future of the game.
Today, we’re sharing more about the future of Bungie, including our plans for Destiny, Marathon, and how we’re changing the way we work. Read more on https://t.co/ZkmLWmaQZr: https://t.co/QbDwADGinr pic.twitter.com/F5tcXF0TsN
Marathon had a rough start since its launch in March; while it received critical acclaim upon release, according to data from SteamsCharts, it currently boasts around 1,390 active players, with a peak of just 2,630 in the last 24 hours. This is merely a small slice of Destiny 2's comparatively massive playerbase, and it seems the team at Bungie has taken notice of this, given its renewed efforts to reshape the game.
Perhaps most importantly, the two also confirmed that no, Marathon is not replacing Destiny, which had its own exciting announcements from the duo in that same video. Players, rejoice; there are "more stories to tell" in the Destiny universe, and Bungie wants to return the series to "its original promise" of "awe-inspiring mystery, the sense of discovery, and the promise of a community of Guardians rallying together, raging against impossible odds."
This comes as welcome news for Destiny fans, as Bungie infamously shuttered future content updates for Destiny 2 in May. The announcement didn't go over well, leaving players equal parts confused and distraught — but it seems the developer has decided against abandoning the IP in the wake of this strong community response.
This double-whammy of exciting announcements comes after major shifts for Bungie over the last few months. PlayStation CEO Herman Hulst confirmed "significant" layoffs for the studio in June, which included "most of the Destiny team and some Marathon team members." The developer also revealed plans to sublease a significant portion of its massive campus in Bellevue, Washington earlier this month.
With its renewed focus on Destiny and a sharper look at the future of Marathon, Bungie appears to be entering a new, exciting era, and fans can't wait to see what it's cooking up next.

item.title: Bungie has said it is "absolutely not done with Destiny" just months after its controversial decision to end ongoing support for Destiny 2.
item.description:
Bungie has said it is "absolutely not done with Destiny" just months after the controversial decision to end ongoing support for Destiny 2.
The five-minute upload features Bungie studio head Poria Torkan and head of product, GM of Marathon Josh Deane. The two executives start their surprise talk with fans, promising that Sony has not completely abandoned the Destiny brand after months of fans pleading to see them either return to Destiny 2 or eventually create Destiny 3.
"We're not asking for your trust," Torkan said, acknowledging some of Bungie's recent struggles. "We know we have to earn it, and to do that, we need our games to deliver in ways that exceed your expectations of what you've come to love about the games that we make – and that starts with Destiny.
Today, we’re sharing more about the future of Bungie, including our plans for Destiny, Marathon, and how we’re changing the way we work. Read more on https://t.co/ZkmLWmaQZr: https://t.co/QbDwADGinr pic.twitter.com/F5tcXF0TsN
"Bungie wouldn't be what it is today without it. It's the foundation upon which everything else rests, and we are absolutely not done with Destiny. We have more stories to tell, but we have to do it right and give our teams the time they need to do justice to this amazing universe."
Deane clarified that Bungie's goal is to "return Destiny to its original promise." That means going back to "awe-inspiring mystery, the sense of discovery, and the promise of a community of Guardians rallying together, raging against impossible odds."
It's been a painful few months for the players who stuck by Destiny and Destiny 2 before substantial support came to an end with the Monument of Triumph update in June. Unfortunately, restoring that community and rebuilding trust will take even more time.
"I wish we could just flip a freaking switch, but we're going to commit to unvaulting the Destiny 2 campaigns, the destinations, the raids that never should have been ripped away to begin with," Deane added. "They were an essential part of our journey together and definitely a place where we built memories with y'all."
Bungie shared additional details with a post on its website. In a segment titled "Destiny Is Foundational to Our Future," the team excplitly called attention to the players who rallied together to give Destiny another shot at life. Through all of the uncertainty, comments, and livestream chat takeovers, it seems those in charge heard fans loud and clear.
"Your voices mattered, and the way you showed up made a real impact," the message said. "You reminded everyone how much this world, its history, and its future still mean to you."
As teased in the video, the first step to a future with more Destiny stories means unvaulting experiences that were previously locked away. The studio acknowledged that the vaulting certain experiences "had a lasting impact on player trust and enjoyment of Destiny," adding that "Destiny 2 is more than just the content itself."
You did not go gentle into that good night.
"It is a place where players have built memories together, formed lasting friendships, and shared experiences that have stayed with them for years. We cannot change the decision we made, but we can acknowledge its impact and do the work to make it right by restoring these important parts of Destiny’s history."
Bungie said it is just getting started on the work required to unvault campaigns, destinations, and raids. All of this content will be made available for "all Destiny 2 players," though the developers caution that "bringing back this content is not as simple as restoring old files."
Changes made post-Beyond Light will require the studio to update lighting, encounters, combatants, and more. It's work that will take time, but the fact the effort is being put in at all is something that will no doubt have fans waiting on the edges of their seats, no matter how long it takes.
"When we look to the future of Destiny all up this restoration is the first step to lay the foundation for how we reforge into new stories and games that you all deserve," the message continued. "We’ll have more details on our unvaulting efforts in the coming months, and we’re very excited to share more about our vision to celebrate Destiny’s legacy and build its future with you all as soon as we can."
So, what exactly does this mean? While fans may not want to get their hopes up that this video serves as confirmation of Destiny 3 quite yet, Deane did say the plan is to deliver "new Destiny stories and games" that players deserve. In other words, the promise of more Destiny, a day many thought may never come, is here.
Aside from the untimely demise of the now-revived Destiny 2, Bungie itself has undergone a wave of significant changes in recent months. In June, the company was confirmed to have been impacted by layoffs affecting almost 300 staff. A few weeks ago, the company confirmed plans to sublease parts of its Bellevue, Washington headquarters.
Will Destiny 2 relaunch with a new name? Will we ever get Destiny 3? Will Bungie get to breathe life into its reported Destiny Infinity idea? Only time will tell, but one thing is certain: Marathon will not be replacing Destiny.
